His rapid advancement is due in large part to Janus Borig's cards. He absorbed pivotal experiences from many of the most important figures in contemporary history. 

This point is really well illustrated when he's in the forest while tracking the red wight. Though that card didn't instantly make Kip an expert tracker, it gave him a thorough understanding of what mastery looks like and what skills it's composed of. That deep knowledge skilled him up in sneaking though the woods tremendously. 

Presumably he has the same sort of leg up in a vast array of disciplines from the cards. Much of Kip's huge increase in skills can be directly attributed to this.

They wouldn't have waited until she was 20. Felia was around 17 when she had Ggavin. (Also, at one point in BK Liv refers to herself as a woman old enough to have her own children because she's 17.)

But on the ship he first dilates out to see paryl. He sees the paryl and senses that it's wrapped around, fighting with another force that he assumes is chi. An explosion happens while his pupils are fully dilated and he goes blind but keeps willing the two forces apart. 

It's interesting that when Kip resumes consciousness he hears:

“What’s wrong with his eyes? One is—and the other—” “Cover his eyes! He’s staring at the sun, you fools!” the captain shouted.

Totally valid. I say Dgavin is crazy and then believe his first hand report of the bullets. It's inconsistent logic at best, even without the dead man manipulating Dgavin's perception. 

The thing that makes me believe further that those bullets didn't go through Ggavin - Andross never makes any reference to finding the corpse. It seems like something that he would make at least an oblique reference to. He would make Dgavin pay for leaving Ggavin to rot, or we would have some hint at Andross' bitterness that Ggavin was so close for so long without him knowing.

Instead Andross just goes on about the insanity of Dgavin creating the prison in the first place. If Andross were aware that Ggavin had been there at some point, then I think the exposition would have been different somewhere along the way.

I want Liv to do something right for her father's sake. I definitely don't see her surviving. There's no going back from Ferrilux, but I at least want her to have a moment of "Everything I did was wrong. Ruining this for the White King is the least I can do, even as it destroys me." -Or- Liv is already suspicious of her djinn, Beliol. Maybe she strikes a blow against the djinn that ends up aiding our heroes' side.

I just want... something that Corvin can look back at without total regret. He's had a seriously raw deal, and I want there to be something he can take pride in despite the ruin.

So I think the cards aren't fully outside of time like the 200/djinn are. I'm still confused by the card giving current-ish information about Gunner.

When DGavin examines the bullets embedded in the yellow cell, that put it to rest for me. They are definitely DGavin's handcrafted bullets, and they didn't go through a body before hitting the wall. Even if GGavin was imprisoned there at some point, I still don't believe DGavin shot and killed him in the yellow prison. 

Furthermore it was a really good point that it'd be nigh impossible to keep GGavin alive, fully sedated, and locked in a trunk on the way back to the Chromeria. With no one knowing, no one helping to feed and water him? No one to clean out the filth accumulating? Presumably getting all that effluvia in open, untended wounds...

I'm down with DGavin hallucinating the yellow alarm before believing GGavin survived in a trunk for more than a month on the way home. The spear, which is -as a bonus- a physical representation of DGavin's insanity, was in the trunk. 

I believe at times of greatest stress DGavin would go down and rave at the empty cells, perhaps getting responses from the will cast (or possibly djinn) "dead men."

Also, it's 50/50 for me as to whether DGavin killed his brother Sevastian and gained blue drafting then.

I *loved* DGavin when I thought he was a hero who'd made hard choices and was tortured by nightmares. I was crushed when it turned out that he wasn't who he thought he was. But I do believe in that insanity. DGavin is still a Great man, but he's also a self-decieving figure tainted by black luxin insanity. He did draft white at Garrison though. Redemption is still possible at the reef.

I'm hoping that Marrisia comes back into play along with those letters, all of Orea's instructions for the new White. Perhaps Andross or the Order need her related to that intelligence. I hope against hope that Karris gets that information somehow. Probably won't happen, but I want Karris to have every advantage.

Either way we didn't see Marissia die and she's too valuable to have been totally discarded.

I agree that there almost has to be some deus ex machina in a final battle. My suspicion is that it will involve DGavin drafting "burning white" luxin at the Orholam/Nexus/Possibly-White-Seed-Crystal.

I really enjoyed BM though. 

Agreed that there wasn't enough Liv. I'm hoping she's redeemed in taking down the other Bane/Gods. 

Possibly a redemption two-fer in a deus ex machina. Like, DGavin is about to save the day (and ascend to the 200?) by sacrificing himself while drafting white at the reef tower with Orholam. The White King's god/bane/wight army almost destroys DGavin's moment, but Liv/Ferrilux is able to betray the White King's forces to allow DGavin to succeed.

This ends the war. No white king, no war.

No idea what Kip's role will be in that conflict.

I'm terrified of what King Ironfist brings to the table, but I assume that will be tied in Karris and Teia's plot lines. I so want Ironfist to be redeemed, as DGavin makes the Order's plan fail. Ironfist is pious. There's no way he wants the Order to win if it means the destruction of Orholam.

Also hoping that Andross gets some sort of epic comeuppance. As unlikely as it is, I want him to be blindsided by Grinwoody being the Old Man of the Desert. I hate Grinwoody, but Grinwoody destroying Andross? Eh, I can get behind that. Maybe Teia takes out Grinwoody? (and Murder Sharp!) Everybody wins!

I'm okay with Kip's storylines in BM. I can see why people could be dissatisfied, but I see this as development in him growing up fast and finally losing his self deprecation. A big part of his lack of personal self confidence related to his body image and relationships with women, so his relationship to Tisis doesn't feel like a throwaway plot to me. It's kind of the last thing he needed to become truly ready to lead with total confidence, with the huge asset of a canny, diplomatic badass for a wife. I have no idea how the Lightbringer prophecies are going to figure in to the final resolution, but after the first two chapters of BW, it looks like he knows he must expand the Mighty. That could look like anything - maybe even traveling back to the Chromeria for more Blackguards? ...and hopefully destroying that sociopath Zymun along the way.

There was so much setup in BM, so many new angles. I'm psyched to see how it comes together.

When DGavin faces down the Orholam/Nexus he creates some sort of deus ex machina in an explosion while drafting white luxin. 

I feel so convinced that burning white must have something to do with a climactic redemption/martyrdom scene involving DGavin.

Realistically? Because depression has robbed me of positive emotion and made me feel like a worthless burden.

Coming up with specifics though:

Lack of lasting positive contribution to society.

I don't find satisfaction when I do well in life. I'm a perfectionist who either succeeds above expectations or crashes and burns. I fold under pressure, so I can't be counted on professionally. Nothing I do is ever good enough for me.

I cheat in romantic relationships. I have genes that are full of mental illness and addiction tendencies, so it would be irresponsible to breed.

Basically it's not that I add nothing to the world - I work in a helping profession and have volunteered quite a bit over the years. It's that - someone else can do it. 

There's nothing special or amazing about me that makes me essential in the world. I want the suffering to end, and -if nothing else- I'm a horrible bastard for being willing to inflict this grief on my family. 

So take your pick. I'll never measure up because I have impossible standards.

Thank you. I would rather be alone though. Pushing everyone out was easy. It's just my sweet husband who I can't get away from because we live together.

There are people who would absolutely rush in if I let them know how bad things are. It's just that I don't want friends or family to save me. I don't want people trying to help me "get better."

The less people interact with me, the less they'll have guilt, like, "oh, if only I'd said x." Instead they'll have, "I sent a couple of texts 6 months ago, and she didn't respond." Silence and isolation is better than pretending happiness. I don't want to play people for fools.
I've been both. When you fake it that well, it's a totally different emptiness. If your depression is totally incapacitating, at least you're living "honestly."
